## Reproducible Research with Quarto

Quarto enables reproducible research by combining code, text, and output in a single document.

### Creating Reports

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

data_1 <- readxl::read_excel("../data/PublicHealth_BP_Dataset.xlsx")
```

### Inline Code

The mean age is `r mean(gtsummary::trial$age)` years.

### Figures

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-dist
#| fig-cap: "Distribution of Age"
ggplot(gtsummary::trial, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "blue", alpha = 0.7) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Tables

```{r}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Summary Statistics"
data_1 %>% 
  summarise(
    Mean_Age = mean(Age),
    SD_Age = sd(Age),
    Mean_SBP = mean(SysBP_0m),
    SD_SBP = sd(SysBP_0m)
  ) %>% 
  knitr::kable()
```

### Citations and References

Quarto supports citations using BibTeX or DOI.

:::
